title: Before the Protest
subtitle: Preparation & Internet Shutdowns
content: • Carry a fully charged phone and a power bank. • Carry a government-issued photo ID. • Bring water, snacks, any essential medications, and weather-appropriate clothing. • Download Offline Google Maps of your city. • Download Bitchat or Briar. These apps use nearby Bluetooth devices to communicate without internet. • Ensure you have an exit location memorised in case of an emergency. • Note down emergency contacts, two lawyers' contacts, and contacts for medical aid. Ideally, write important phone numbers on your arm using a permanent marker. • Switch backup cloud storage to automatic. • Attend with a buddy or a group whenever possible. • Download the Solidarity Kit (works offline and self-updates when your phone is connected to the internet again).

title: During the Protest
subtitle: Stay Safe
content:
• Stay with your group.

• Remain aware of exits and safe routes.

• Avoid escalating confrontations.

• Document incidents only when it is safe to do so.

• Keep your phone charged and use it responsibly.

title: If Detained
subtitle: Know Your Rights
content:
• Stay calm.

• Ask whether you are under arrest and why.

• Ask which police station you are being taken to.

• Request access to a lawyer.

• Inform a trusted contact or family member as soon as possible.

• Refer to the 'Know Your Rights' section on the home page for detailed legal information.

title: After the Protest
subtitle: Follow-Up & Documentation
content:
• Your health comes first. Take care of any immediate medical needs. Refer to the Medical Aid and Mental Health sections for available resources.

• Account for everyone you attended the protest with. Leave no one behind. If someone cannot be located or contacted, use trusted social media networks to help locate them.

• Download and securely store all videos, photos, and voice recordings for legal or medical purposes.

• Back up all evidence to cloud storage as soon as internet access is available.
